\"I\'ve seen them early\" turns the warning on even outside their typical season — it turns off by itself in a few weeks if no one else confirms it.
Confirmed — thanks for letting us know.

There\'s no reliable map of where pine processionary caterpillars are — the only way to know is if someone has seen them. If you see them here, mark \"Yes, they\'re in this sector\": the school will keep warning every season, with no one having to report it again.

These are pine processionary caterpillars, active mostly in winter and spring. Their hairs are urticant: they cause itching and allergy in people, but can be very serious for dogs — if a dog touches or licks them, its tongue can swell and even necrotize, sometimes requiring amputation to save it. Keep your dog away from the nests (white bags on branches) and from caterpillars on the ground.
They\'ve been seen here in other years, but we\'re currently outside their typical season (roughly December-May).
⚠ They\'ve been seen at this school before, and we\'re in their typical season (roughly) — take extra care, especially with dogs.

\"Yes, they\'re in this sector\" marks the school forever: every December-May it will warn on its own, with no one having to repeat it. \"I\'ve seen them early\" turns the warning on NOW, even outside those months. Both can be toggled on and off — if you tap by mistake, tap again to remove it.
